Probability forecasts as martingales

A sequence of forecasts for one event must agree about what future information can reveal. We first prove that conditional event probabilities form a martingale, then construct two diffusion models and derive a bound on expected squared revisions. The models also show why a claim about “more uncertainty” needs to specify which quantity changes.

The calibration page supplies the binary payoff and Brier score; probability conflation explains why event accuracy does not identify severity. Here the payoff is exactly one or zero. Source context is SCoFT v4, chapter 14, pp. 261–273 Taleb, 2025; the chapter guide records qualifications and locators. Every numerical example is synthetic.

One event, one probability law¶

Fix a probability space with law PPP, an increasing filtration (Ft)0≤t≤T(\mathcal F_t)_{0\le t\le T}(Ft​)0≤t≤T​, and an event A∈FTA\in\mathcal F_TA∈FT​. A filtration records all information retained by the forecaster at each time. Define the report

pt=E[1A∣Ft].p_t=\mathbb E[\mathbf1_A\mid\mathcal F_t].pt​=E[1A​∣Ft​].
(1)

The shared notation uses PPP for the law and E\mathbb EE for its expectation. Our local ptp_tpt​ is an event probability, not a density. Conditional expectations are understood up to almost-sure equality. Since 0≤1A≤10\le\mathbf1_A\le10≤1A​≤1, each ptp_tpt​ is integrable, lies in [0,1][0,1][0,1], and pT=1Ap_T=\mathbf1_ApT​=1A​.

Martingale identity. For s≤ts\le ts≤t, the tower property gives

E[pt∣Fs]=E[E[1A∣Ft]∣Fs]=E[1A∣Fs]=ps.\begin{aligned} \mathbb E[p_t\mid\mathcal F_s] &=\mathbb E[\mathbb E[\mathbf1_A\mid\mathcal F_t] \mid\mathcal F_s]\\ &=\mathbb E[\mathbf1_A\mid\mathcal F_s]=p_s. \end{aligned}E[pt​∣Fs​]​=E[E[1A​∣Ft​]∣Fs​]=E[1A​∣Fs​]=ps​.​
(2)

This proves the claim under the forecaster’s own law. It also holds in the smaller filtration Gt=σ(pr:r≤t)\mathcal G_t=\sigma(p_r:r\le t)Gt​=σ(pr​:r≤t) generated by the reports: apply the tower property again, using psp_sps​’s Gs\mathcal G_sGs​-measurability. Conversely, an adapted martingale with terminal value 1A\mathbf1_A1A​ has pt=E[1A∣Ft]p_t=\mathbb E[\mathbf1_A\mid\mathcal F_t]pt​=E[1A​∣Ft​] by its defining identity. Boundedness or a constant unconditional mean alone does not imply this conditional identity.

The claim requires the same event, law, and nested information sets. Replacing the event, forgetting information, or changing the model without embedding that change in one joint law does not satisfy these assumptions. Ordinary conditional expectation is the only prerequisite; see the conditional-expectation note.

Fair bets, scores, and market prices¶

We prove two finite-horizon consequences of the identity. On a deterministic grid t0<⋯<tm=Tt_0<\cdots<t_m=Tt0​<⋯<tm​=T, let hih_ihi​ be a bounded Fti\mathcal F_{t_i}Fti​​-measurable position. A purchase of hih_ihi​ units at ptip_{t_i}pti​​, unwound at the next quote, has gain

Δpi=pti+1−pti,G=∑i=0m−1hiΔpi,E[hiΔpi]=0,E[G]=0.\begin{gathered} \Delta p_i=p_{t_{i+1}}-p_{t_i},\\ G=\sum_{i=0}^{m-1}h_i\Delta p_i,\\ \mathbb E[h_i\Delta p_i]=0,\qquad \mathbb E[G]=0. \end{gathered}Δpi​=pti+1​​−pti​​,G=i=0∑m−1​hi​Δpi​,E[hi​Δpi​]=0,E[G]=0.​
(3)

Condition first on Fti\mathcal F_{t_i}Fti​​ to prove the third equality, then sum. Such a gain cannot be nonnegative almost surely and positive with positive probability. This is a precise no-free-lunch statement for bounded predictable positions under PPP. It assumes two-way execution at the quotes, no transaction costs, zero financing rate, and self-financing trades. It says nothing about unbounded doubling strategies.

De Finetti’s probability-assessor connection is that the quoted probability is a price at which either side of a unit event bet is acceptable. For finitely many fair bets, a common expectation precludes a strictly positive gain in every outcome. This proves the needed implication from probability coherence to fair betting; it is not a proof of the full representation theorem for coherent assessments. Chapter 14, §14.3, pp. 269–271 supplies the historical connection Taleb, 2025.

For an Ft\mathcal F_tFt​-measurable report qt∈[0,1]q_t\in[0,1]qt​∈[0,1], the conditional version of the existing Brier calculation is

E[(1A−qt)2∣Ft]=pt(1−pt)+(qt−pt)2.\begin{aligned} \mathbb E[(\mathbf1_A-q_t)^2\mid\mathcal F_t] &=p_t(1-p_t)\\ &\quad+(q_t-p_t)^2. \end{aligned}E[(1A​−qt​)2∣Ft​]​=pt​(1−pt​)+(qt​−pt​)2.​
(4)

Expand the square and substitute E[1A∣Ft]=pt\mathbb E[\mathbf1_A\mid\mathcal F_t]=p_tE[1A​∣Ft​]=pt​ to prove it. The unique minimizing report is ptp_tpt​. Thus optimal conditional quadratic scoring and dynamic fair betting select the same conditional probability under the specified law. Linear trading profit is not itself a strictly proper score.

A traded claim can instead be valued under a pricing law QQQ. If its discounted price is a conditional expectation under QQQ, the martingale identity is under QQQ; identifying QQQ with a physical or subjective law PPP is an additional assumption. Complementary prices summing to one do not force that identification. A predictable positive expected gain under PPP can still incur losses, so it is not automatically an arbitrage. For example, if P(A)=0.6P(A)=0.6P(A)=0.6 but two complementary claims both cost 0.5, their prices sum to one. Buying the first has expected gain 0.1 under PPP, but loses 0.5 when the event fails.

Gaussian terminal uncertainty¶

For a local approximation to a vote-share estimate, take Xt=x0+σWtX_t=x_0+\sigma W_tXt​=x0​+σWt​ with constant σ>0\sigma>0σ>0 and standard Brownian motion WWW under PPP. Use its usual filtration, a fixed threshold uuu, and A={XT>u}A=\{X_T>u\}A={XT​>u}. This model allows values outside [0,1][0,1][0,1]; it is an approximation to a proportion, not an exactly bounded share process. At t<Tt<Tt<T, put τ=T−t\tau=T-tτ=T−t, s=στs=\sigma\sqrt\taus=στ​ and d=(x−u)/sd=(x-u)/sd=(x−u)/s. The independent normal increment gives

XT∣Xt=x ∼N(x,s2),p(t,x)=Φ(d),d=x−us.\begin{gathered} X_T\mid X_t=x\ \sim N(x,s^2),\\ p(t,x)=\Phi(d),\qquad d=\frac{x-u}{s}. \end{gathered}XT​∣Xt​=x ∼N(x,s2),p(t,x)=Φ(d),d=sx−u​.​
(5)

This is the undiscounted value of a binary Bachelier claim. It follows by standardizing the terminal inequality and using normal symmetry. Here Φ\PhiΦ is the standard normal CDF and ϕ=Φ′\phi=\Phi'ϕ=Φ′ its density. Differentiation at fixed x,ux,ux,u yields

∂p∂s=−dϕ(d)s,∂p∂x=ϕ(d)s,∂p∂τ=−dϕ(d)2τ.\begin{gathered} \frac{\partial p}{\partial s} =-\frac{d\phi(d)}{s},\\ \frac{\partial p}{\partial x} =\frac{\phi(d)}{s},\qquad \frac{\partial p}{\partial\tau} =-\frac{d\phi(d)}{2\tau}. \end{gathered}∂s∂p​=−sdϕ(d)​,∂x∂p​=sϕ(d)​,∂τ∂p​=−2τdϕ(d)​.​
(6)

Increasing the remaining normal standard deviation moves the report toward 1/21/21/2, on either side of the threshold. The limit as s→∞s\to\inftys→∞ is 1/21/21/2. The level sensitivity ϕ(d)/s\phi(d)/sϕ(d)/s tends to zero, but increases when s<∣x−u∣s<|x-u|s<∣x−u∣ and decreases when s>∣x−u∣s>|x-u|s>∣x−u∣. Decreasing τ\tauτ at fixed x≠ux\ne ux=u sharpens the report toward zero or one. At x=ux=ux=u and positive sss the probability is 1/21/21/2. At zero variance we use the strict-event value 1{x>u}\mathbf1_{\{x>u\}}1{x>u}​, including zero at the tie; that degenerate case differs from the positive-variance limit.

Sensitivity to the underlying level is not the same as the forecast’s instantaneous volatility. Applying Itô’s formula gives diffusion coefficient σ∂xp=ϕ(d)/τ\sigma\partial_xp=\phi(d)/\sqrt\tauσ∂x​p=ϕ(d)/τ​. Its drift is zero: ∂tp=dϕ(d)/(2τ)\partial_t p=d\phi(d)/(2\tau)∂t​p=dϕ(d)/(2τ) and ∂xxp=−dϕ(d)/s2\partial_{xx}p=-d\phi(d)/s^2∂xx​p=−dϕ(d)/s2 cancel in ∂tp+σ2∂xxp/2\partial_t p+\sigma^2\partial_{xx}p/2∂t​p+σ2∂xx​p/2 for t<Tt<Tt<T. At the threshold it is independent of σ\sigmaσ; away from it, it increases toward that same value as σ\sigmaσ increases. There is therefore no universal rule that a higher underlying volatility lowers forecast-path volatility.

Use gaussian_binary_probability to compare remaining horizons and the deterministic boundary.

from xmath.incerto.martingales import gaussian_binary_probability

for tau in (1, .25, .01, 0):
    p = gaussian_binary_probability(.54, .08, tau)
    print(f"time left={tau:.2f}: probability={p:.3f}")
print(f"deterministic tie: {gaussian_binary_probability(.5, 0, 1):.1f}")

Output

time left=0.25: probability=0.841
time left=0.01: probability=1.000
time left=0.00: probability=1.000
deterministic tie: 0.0

An exactly bounded share process¶

We now construct a different model. Write Yt∈(0,1)Y_t\in(0,1)Yt​∈(0,1) for the share; YYY is local to this page, not the positive mixing variable of the Normix notation. Its unbounded coordinate is Zt=Φ−1(Yt)Z_t=\Phi^{-1}(Y_t)Zt​=Φ−1(Yt​). Fix σ>0\sigma>0σ>0, deterministic Z0=z0∈RZ_0=z_0\in\mathbb RZ0​=z0​∈R, and Brownian motion WWW under PPP, with its usual filtration. Define

Zt=eσ2t/2(z0+σ∫0te−σ2r/2 dWr),Yt=Φ(Zt).\begin{gathered} Z_t=e^{\sigma^2t/2}\left(z_0+\sigma \int_0^t e^{-\sigma^2r/2}\,dW_r\right),\\ Y_t=\Phi(Z_t). \end{gathered}Zt​=eσ2t/2(z0​+σ∫0t​e−σ2r/2dWr​),Yt​=Φ(Zt​).​
(7)

Equivalently, dZt=12σ2Zt dt+σ dWtdZ_t=\tfrac12\sigma^2Z_t\,dt+\sigma\,dW_tdZt​=21​σ2Zt​dt+σdWt​. The drift is directed away from zero. The explicit solution is finite at every finite time, so the transformed share stays strictly between its endpoints. For h>0h>0h>0, conditional on Zt=zZ_t=zZt​=z, independent Brownian increments give

Zt+h∼N(eσ2h/2z, eσ2h−1).Z_{t+h}\sim N(e^{\sigma^2h/2}z,\ e^{\sigma^2h}-1).Zt+h​∼N(eσ2h/2z, eσ2h−1).
(8)

Here and below the second normal parameter is the variance. This follows by integrating σ2eσ2(h−r)\sigma^2e^{\sigma^2(h-r)}σ2eσ2(h−r) over 0≤r≤h0\le r\le h0≤r≤h.

Bounded martingale proof. For independent standard normals H,NH,NH,N, any real bbb and c≥0c\ge0c≥0,

E[Φ(b+cN)]=P(H−cN≤b)=Φ ⁣(b1+c2).\begin{aligned} \mathbb E[\Phi(b+cN)] &=P(H-cN\le b)\\ &=\Phi\!\left(\frac{b}{\sqrt{1+c^2}}\right). \end{aligned}E[Φ(b+cN)]​=P(H−cN≤b)=Φ(1+c2​b​).​
(9)

Take b=eσ2h/2zb=e^{\sigma^2h/2}zb=eσ2h/2z and c2=eσ2h−1c^2=e^{\sigma^2h}-1c2=eσ2h−1. The denominator is eσ2h/2e^{\sigma^2h/2}eσ2h/2, so E[Yt+h∣Ft]=Φ(z)=Yt\mathbb E[Y_{t+h}\mid\mathcal F_t]=\Phi(z)=Y_tE[Yt+h​∣Ft​]=Φ(z)=Yt​. This proves a true bounded martingale directly from its transition law, without assuming that a nonlinear transform preserves martingales. Itô’s formula gives the equivalent drift cancellation:

ϕ′(z)=−zϕ(z),12σ2zϕ(z)+12σ2ϕ′(z)=0,dYt=σϕ(Zt) dWt.\begin{gathered} \phi'(z)=-z\phi(z),\\ \tfrac12\sigma^2z\phi(z)+\tfrac12\sigma^2\phi'(z)=0,\\ dY_t=\sigma\phi(Z_t)\,dW_t. \end{gathered}ϕ′(z)=−zϕ(z),21​σ2zϕ(z)+21​σ2ϕ′(z)=0,dYt​=σϕ(Zt​)dWt​.​
(10)

Only YYY is a martingale here. In general E[Zt+h∣Ft]=eσ2h/2Zt≠Zt\mathbb E[Z_{t+h}\mid\mathcal F_t]=e^{\sigma^2h/2}Z_t\ne Z_tE[Zt+h​∣Ft​]=eσ2h/2Zt​=Zt​. Even starting at z0=0z_0=0z0​=0 makes just the unconditional mean constant; at positive times the conditional equality fails.

More generally, let S:R→(0,1)S:\mathbb R\to(0,1)S:R→(0,1) be increasing, twice continuously differentiable, and have S′>0S'>0S′>0. For a nonexplosive diffusion dZt=b(Zt)dt+σdWtdZ_t=b(Z_t)dt+\sigma dW_tdZt​=b(Zt​)dt+σdWt​, Itô’s drift vanishes when

b(z)=−σ2S′′(z)2S′(z).b(z)=-\frac{\sigma^2S''(z)}{2S'(z)}.b(z)=−2S′(z)σ2S′′(z)​.
(11)

Localizing the resulting stochastic integral makes S(Z)S(Z)S(Z) a local martingale; its bound by one allows dominated convergence in the stopped conditional identities, making it a true martingale. This assertion assumes the solution exists without explosion on the horizon. For the logistic S(z)=(1+e−z)−1S(z)=(1+e^{-z})^{-1}S(z)=(1+e−z)−1 the required drift is b(z)=σ2(2S(z)−1)/2b(z)=\sigma^2(2S(z)-1)/2b(z)=σ2(2S(z)−1)/2, which is bounded and globally Lipschitz. A sigmoid applied to driftless Brownian motion generally has nonzero Itô drift. Symmetry at its starting point does not remove that drift along subsequent paths.

For a direct counterexample, take Zt=σWtZ_t=\sigma W_tZt​=σWt​ and Yt=Φ(Zt)Y_t=\Phi(Z_t)Yt​=Φ(Zt​), starting at Z0=0Z_0=0Z0​=0. The same normal identity gives, for h>0h>0h>0,

E[Yt]=1/2,E[Yt+h∣Ft]=Φ ⁣(Zt1+σ2h).\begin{gathered} \mathbb E[Y_t]=1/2,\\ \mathbb E[Y_{t+h}\mid\mathcal F_t] =\Phi\!\left(\frac{Z_t}{\sqrt{1+\sigma^2h}}\right). \end{gathered}E[Yt​]=1/2,E[Yt+h​∣Ft​]=Φ(1+σ2h​Zt​​).​
(12)

At any t>0t>0t>0, Zt≠0Z_t\ne0Zt​=0 almost surely, so the latter quantity differs from YtY_tYt​. This proves that the midpoint exception is a statement about the unconditional mean, not the martingale property.

The event probability is a second martingale¶

Fix a share threshold 0<u<10<u<10<u<1, let k=Φ−1(u)k=\Phi^{-1}(u)k=Φ−1(u), and consider A={YT>u}A=\{Y_T>u\}A={YT​>u}. Monotonicity makes this exactly {ZT>k}\{Z_T>k\}{ZT​>k}. For τ>0\tau>0τ>0, the transition law above gives

z=Φ−1(y),p(t,y)=Φ ⁣(z−e−σ2τ/2k1−e−σ2τ).\begin{gathered} z=\Phi^{-1}(y),\\ p(t,y)=\Phi\!\left( \frac{z-e^{-\sigma^2\tau/2}k} {\sqrt{1-e^{-\sigma^2\tau}}}\right). \end{gathered}z=Φ−1(y),p(t,y)=Φ(1−e−σ2τ​z−e−σ2τ/2k​).​
(13)

We obtained this by dividing the terminal normal mean, threshold, and standard deviation by eσ2τ/2e^{\sigma^2\tau/2}eσ2τ/2. The forecast p(t,Yt)p(t,Y_t)p(t,Yt​) is a martingale by the tower proof, and its terminal value is the indicator. The share YtY_tYt​ has terminal value YTY_TYT​, so these are different martingales. Neither statement makes the coordinate ZtZ_tZt​ a martingale. Computing the event in either coordinate must give the same probability; the threshold must be transformed as well.

For a majority threshold u=1/2u=1/2u=1/2, k=0k=0k=0. At fixed interior share yyy, increasing the integrated latent variance σ2τ\sigma^2\tauσ2τ moves p(t,y)p(t,y)p(t,y) toward yyy, and

lim⁡σ2τ→∞p(t,y)=y.\lim_{\sigma^2\tau\to\infty}p(t,y)=y.σ2τ→∞lim​p(t,y)=y.
(14)

Indeed the denominator increases to one, so the argument of Φ\PhiΦ approaches zzz. For y>1/2y>1/2y>1/2 the forecast stays between yyy and one; for y<1/2y<1/2y<1/2 it stays between zero and yyy. For any fixed interior threshold the same limit holds because e−σ2τ/2k→0e^{-\sigma^2\tau/2}k\to0e−σ2τ/2k→0, although monotonicity in σ2τ\sigma^2\tauσ2τ need not. This bounded model therefore does not have a universal 1/21/21/2 limit. Its increasing terminal dispersion preserves the mean share, unlike an unbounded normal approximation with arbitrarily large variance.

Use probit_binary_probability for the bounded model. The noise parameter is in the latent coordinate; it is not the share’s instantaneous volatility, which is σϕ(Φ−1(y))\sigma\phi(\Phi^{-1}(y))σϕ(Φ−1(y)).

How much revision is coherent?¶

Return to any conditional binary forecast, without a diffusion assumption. Fix a deterministic grid ending at resolution, write pi=ptip_i=p_{t_i}pi​=pti​​, and define V=∑i=0m−1(Δpi)2V=\sum_{i=0}^{m-1}(\Delta p_i)^2V=∑i=0m−1​(Δpi​)2. We prove the conditional revision budget and its Brier interpretation:

E[V∣Ft0]=p0(1−p0),E[(1A−pi)2]−E[(1A−pi+1)2]=E[(Δpi)2].\begin{gathered} \mathbb E[V\mid\mathcal F_{t_0}] =p_0(1-p_0),\\ \mathbb E[(\mathbf1_A-p_i)^2] -\mathbb E[(\mathbf1_A-p_{i+1})^2]\\ =\mathbb E[(\Delta p_i)^2]. \end{gathered}E[V∣Ft0​​]=p0​(1−p0​),E[(1A​−pi​)2]−E[(1A​−pi+1​)2]=E[(Δpi​)2].​
(15)

Expand pi+12−pi2=2piΔpi+(Δpi)2p_{i+1}^2-p_i^2=2p_i\Delta p_i+(\Delta p_i)^2pi+12​−pi2​=2pi​Δpi​+(Δpi​)2. The cross term has conditional mean zero. Sum and condition at t0t_0t0​; pm2=1Ap_m^2=\mathbf1_Apm2​=1A​ and E[1A∣Ft0]=p0\mathbb E[\mathbf1_A\mid\mathcal F_{t_0}]=p_0E[1A​∣Ft0​​]=p0​ give the first identity. For the second, expand 1A−pi=(1A−pi+1)+Δpi\mathbf1_A-p_i=(\mathbf1_A-p_{i+1})+\Delta p_i1A​−pi​=(1A​−pi+1​)+Δpi​ and condition the cross term on Fti+1\mathcal F_{t_{i+1}}Fti+1​​; its mean is zero. This proves both formulas.

If the grid stops before resolution, its expected squared revisions, conditional on Ft0\mathcal F_{t_0}Ft0​​, are at most p0(1−p0)p_0(1-p_0)p0​(1−p0​). The missing amount is the expected remaining conditional variance, also conditional on Ft0\mathcal F_{t_0}Ft0​​. More generally the same argument starts at any grid time, conditional on its information. A probability already near zero or one has little expected revision left.

The budget is an expectation, not a pathwise ceiling. A coherent path can fluctuate more than this number, and large news can cause a large single jump. For a continuous martingale, refining the grid yields quadratic-variation increment [p]T−[p]t0[p]_T-[p]_{t_0}[p]T​−[p]t0​​ and the same conditional expectation identity. That continuous-time formulation uses the usual quadratic-variation theorem Karatzas & Shreve, 1991; the finite-grid proof above is complete and is what our diagnostics use. An unstopped Brownian motion with a nonzero constant diffusion cannot remain bounded in [0,1][0,1][0,1] almost surely even on a fixed positive horizon.

A pathwise trading calculation¶

For any quoted path in [0,1][0,1][0,1], the predictable position hi=2(p0−pi)h_i=2(p_0-p_i)hi​=2(p0​−pi​) has exact discrete gain

G=∑i2(p0−pi)Δpi,G=V−(pm−p0)2.\begin{gathered} G=\sum_i2(p_0-p_i)\Delta p_i,\\ G=V-(p_m-p_0)^2. \end{gathered}G=i∑​2(p0​−pi​)Δpi​,G=V−(pm​−p0​)2.​
(16)

To prove it, expand successive squared distances from p0p_0p0​ and telescope. Thus, for deterministic p0p_0p0​, a model promising

V>max⁡{p02,(1−p0)2}almost surelyV>\max\{p_0^2,(1-p_0)^2\} \quad\hbox{almost surely}V>max{p02​,(1−p0​)2}almost surely
(17)

would permit a strictly positive terminal gain in every possible path up to null events, under the execution assumptions above. At every intermediate grid time the gain is at least minus the same maximum, because accumulated squared increments are nonnegative. The strategy therefore has bounded downside as well as bounded holdings. This is a sufficient arbitrage condition, much stronger than an unusually large realized VVV on one observed path. In particular the expectation budget p0(1−p0)p_0(1-p_0)p0​(1−p0​) is not this pathwise bound.

Synthetic paths and diagnostics¶

The simulator samples the exact normal transitions of ZZZ, then maps to the share and its terminal-event probability. It includes resolution as the final forecast column. There is no Euler step or clipping scheme used to enforce the martingale. Floating-point CDF values can round to endpoints; subsequent steps use the retained latent coordinate, never an inverse of the rounded share.

The example uses simulate_probit_forecasts and forecast_revision_summary. Rows are 4,000 independent model paths, with 40 transitions, PCG64 seed 1401, initial share 0.54, latent scale 0.8, horizon one, and threshold 1/21/21/2. The diagnostic compares the average squared revisions with the budget and reports its Monte Carlo standard error across independent rows.

Code: exact paths and the revision budget
from xmath.incerto.martingales import (
    simulate_probit_forecasts, forecast_revision_summary,
)

sample = simulate_probit_forecasts(.54, .8, 1, steps=40,
                                  paths=4000, seed=1401)
report = forecast_revision_summary(sample["probability"])
print(f"initial probability: {sample['probability'][0, 0]:.3f}")
print(f"mean terminal outcome: {sample['outcome'].mean():.3f}")
print(f"squared revisions: {report['squared_revision']:.4f}")
print(f"initial budget: {report['initial_budget']:.4f}")
print(f"gap: {report['budget_gap']:.4f}; SE: {report['budget_gap_se']:.4f}")

Output

initial probability: 0.558
mean terminal outcome: 0.560
squared revisions: 0.2481
initial budget: 0.2466
gap: 0.0015; SE: 0.0034

A conditional identity implies E[h(pi)Δpi]=0\mathbb E[h(p_i)\Delta p_i]=0E[h(pi​)Δpi​]=0 for every bounded measurable hhh. The helper reports both h=1h=1h=1 and h(p)=p−1/2h(p)=p-1/2h(p)=p−1/2, with standard errors computed across independent, identically distributed paths separately at each time. These are necessary moment checks, not sufficient tests of the full filtration. The squared-revision budget adds a different necessary check. Standard errors use the usual i.i.d.-row formula; independence alone does not justify pooling rows with different means. Adjacent times on one election path are not independent events. Selecting a statistic after looking at many dates also changes any inferential interpretation.

For a controlled failure, alternate adding and subtracting 0.12 from interior forecasts and clip to [0,1][0,1][0,1], retaining the original initial and terminal reports. This deliberately altered sequence is not the conditional probability under the simulation law. The experiment compares its squared revisions and scores with those of the coherent model; it makes no claim about actual election predictions.

Regenerate all three figures with uv run python demos/incerto/forecast_martingales.py. They use the common figure exporter and fixed seeds. The formulas and finite-grid proofs establish coherence under their stated models; the simulations check numerical implementations and illustrate sampling variation. Marginal calibration, a few small moment residuals, or one smooth-looking forecast path cannot establish dynamic coherence.

Sources and scope¶

SCoFT v4 §14.0.1, pp. 263–264 and §14.1, pp. 266–267 motivate binary valuation; §14.2, pp. 268–269 supplies the bounded-transform construction; §14.3, pp. 269–271 connects probability assessment with scoring; §14.4 and its addendum, pp. 271–273 motivate revision constraints Taleb, 2025. Our derivations distinguish the Gaussian and bounded limits, preserve the transformed threshold, and separate a constant mean from a martingale. Itô’s formula and the continuous quadratic-variation theorem are used as stochastic-calculus prerequisites, not proved here. No empirical forecaster assessment or general claim that uncertainty forces a probability to 1/21/21/2 follows from these calculations.
